It is structurally dual to the Brier score, with both metrics quantifying the same underlying property of probabilistic forecasts but through complementary lenses: variance versus bias. In the context of GSE's public-facing API, this operator enforces the 'public/private doctrine' by ensuring that all disclosed projections have been verified against realized outcomes, thereby preventing the leakage of internal model parameters or proprietary algorithms. The operator's breakdown regime at extreme over- or under-confidence ($\mathcal{C} \rightarrow 0$ or $\infty$) acts as an anti-collinearity veto: if a model exhibits such behavior, it indicates either data snooping or reliance on non-public features, which would violate compliance standards. Thus, calibration serves as both a performance metric and a gatekeeper for responsible distribution.
